Try this. Refine the grid. The left sum approaches \(\tfrac12W_1^2-\tfrac12\), rather than \(\tfrac12W_1^2\). A new sample changes the endpoint and the integral.

Exact finite identity: \(\sum_i W_{t_i}\Delta W_i=\tfrac12 W_T^2-\tfrac12 Q_n\). The limiting correction is \(T/2\). This example is algebraically exact at finite resolution; its reference limit is a different quantity.

Try this. Set \(\theta=0\): the model becomes scaled Brownian motion. Increase \(\theta\) and the variance levels off. Set the noise to zero to watch a deterministic exponential return. The preferred level is zero.

Exact Gaussian OU transitions at 160 grid steps; \(X_0=x_0,\ m=0\). For \(\theta\) > 0, \(\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=\frac{\sigma^2}{2\theta}(1-e^{-2\theta t})\). The continuous limit at \(\theta=0\) is \(\sigma^2t\).

A fair independent coin model, simulated with seeded draws. “Replay this sequence” clears the revealed steps and lets you reveal the same outcomes again. “Draw a new sequence” selects a fresh set of outcomes and returns to the start; its sequence number changes.
